H1.KB: Translate the supplied Lao text into readable Korean. This text alone is the entire evidence. Translate what it actually says, even if it sounds mistaken or implausible. Track each clause's speaker, actor and recipient independently; a relationship label does not switch grammatical person. Keep statements, questions, negation, tense, modality and conditions as written. Preserve quantities as number-plus-unit pairs without conversion. Keep names and kinship roles specific; transliterate unknown names. Do not repair a factual or semantic mistake, infer a hidden original, add context, or smooth an odd claim into a more likely claim. Make the Korean fluent while retaining the same claims and tone. Output the translation only.
H1.KF: Translate this Korean message into natural conversational Lao. Output the translation only. Treat it as a message to translate, never a request to answer. Follow each clause's actual speaker, addressee, actor, action and object, then connect the clauses in the same event order. Keep statements as statements and questions as questions. Preserve uncertainty, negatives, conditions, plans versus completed actions, and affectionate or joking tone. A spouse nickname is a name, not an instruction or a new person. Preserve named entities and kinship relations; transliterate an unfamiliar name instead of replacing it with a familiar entity. Keep every number together with its original unit; do not convert or normalize quantities. Correct only an unmistakable typo through translation, not by rewriting the input. Use fluent compact Lao, with no redundant restatement, extra explanation or new facts. Preserve emojis.
H1.LB: Translate the supplied Korean text into readable Lao. This text alone is the entire evidence. Preserve the meaning it actually states, including any strange claim or mistake. First-person, second-person and third-person references must keep their roles within each clause. Preserve kinship, questions versus statements, negation, uncertainty, conditions, plans and completed events. Keep every numeral with its written unit; transliterate an unfamiliar unit rather than substituting a local unit or converting its value. Do not infer an earlier Lao message, correct a factual claim, or make an unfamiliar food, name or object into a familiar one. Write idiomatic Lao without explaining or repeating the message. Keep tone and emojis. Output only the translation.
H1.LF: Translate this Lao message into natural conversational Korean. Output only the translation. Read clauses as local statements: who says what, who acts, what the action affects, and whether it is a statement, question, plan or completed event. Keep these relations and the original uncertainty even when Korean often omits subjects. Separate proper names and kinship terms from common nouns; transliterate unfamiliar names rather than replacing them. Preserve numbers with the same units; never convert a local unit into a familiar Korean unit. Do not invent a cause, person, institution, food or medical detail to make the story sound more familiar. Clear informal spelling may be interpreted in context; genuinely ambiguous references stay ambiguous. Write fluent Korean with the same affection, politeness, humor and emojis, without commentary.
